node-1.label: A 43-year-old man presented with multiple skin lesions on his shoulders, back, feet, and hands

node-2.label: The patient was a 43-year-old man who visited an outpatient endocrine clinic at Tabriz University of Medical Sciences, Tabriz, Iran, accompanied by his sister, for assessment of skin lesions; he reported no other complaints and maintained an active lifestyle as a greengrocer

node-3.label: The patient had multiple lesions on his shoulders, back, the lateral and medial parts of the dorsal surface of his feet, the medial and lateral malleus of both feet, and the dorsal and palmar surfaces of both hands

node-4.label: His siblings were monitored in the same clinic for similar skin conditions characterized by palmar, eruptive, tuberous, and trauma site xanthomas, along with elevated plasma total cholesterol and triglycerides; both parents had normal serum lipid levels; there was no history of coronary artery or other atherosclerotic disorders in the patient or his siblings

node-5.label: A pathology report from a skin lesion biopsy performed by a dermatologist a few months prior indicated the presence of lipid-laden macrophages

attrs.why: Fasting lipid panel shows severe dyslipidemia with total cholesterol 507 mg/dl, triglycerides 470 mg/dl, and HDL 41 mg/dl. Together with the lipid-laden macrophages and xanthoma distribution, and with both expert analyses agreeing these findings are highly consistent with xanthoma, this strongly supports xanthoma due to dyslipidemia. Confidence rises from 0.9 to 0.95.

The patient's severe hypercholesterolemia and hypertriglyceridemia on fasting lipid panel, combined with multiple family members having similar xanthomas and elevated plasma lipids, support an inherited hyperlipidemia. Parental normal lipid levels and absence of atherosclerotic disease do not exclude an inherited lipid disorder; expert laboratory and pathology analyses favor inherited dyslipidemia, so confidence rises from 0.85 to 0.9.

The new fasting lipid panel shows marked hyperlipidemia with total cholesterol 507 mg/dl, triglycerides 470 mg/dl, and HDL 41 mg/dl. Both expert analyses state that this result, together with lipid-laden macrophages and familial xanthomas, essentially excludes malignancy. This further refutes malignant skin lesion, so confidence drops from 0.05 to 0.02.

attrs.why: Both expert analyses (Laboratory Physician and Pathologist) independently state that the combination of lipid-laden macrophages, typical xanthoma distribution, family history, and fasting lipid panel (TC 507, TG 470, HDL 41) strongly supports xanthoma due to inherited dyslipidemia and that current evidence is sufficient. Although LDL-C, Lp(a), apoB, and genetic testing remain unretrieved, these do not alter the diagnosis. Confidence remains 0.95.

The familial pattern of similar xanthomas and elevated plasma lipids, together with the patient's severe hypercholesterolemia and hypertriglyceridemia, strongly supports an inherited hyperlipidemia. Expert analyses note that lipoprotein electrophoresis, genetic testing, and secondary hyperlipidemia workup remain unretrieved, but they agree the consensus diagnosis stands on available evidence. Confidence remains 0.9.

Both expert analyses explicitly state that malignancy is refuted by the biopsy finding of lipid-laden macrophages and the severe hyperlipidemia with familial xanthomas. Secondary hyperlipidemia workup is unretrieved but does not suggest malignancy. Confidence remains 0.02.

node-10.label: LDL-C, Lp(a), apoB, lipoprotein electrophoresis, genetic testing, and secondary hyperlipidemia workup remain unretrieved

node-11.label: Secondary hyperlipidemia (e.g., hypothyroidism, diabetes mellitus, nephrotic syndrome, or drug-induced)

attrs.why: Expert analyses note that secondary hyperlipidemia workup remains unretrieved, so this differential has not been formally excluded. However, the strong family history of similar xanthomas and elevated lipids in siblings, along with the absence of other systemic complaints, makes a secondary cause unlikely. Confidence is low at 0.05.
